findings.title: A dry run saves the Qodo re-ask as done, so the real run never asks and stops
findings.why: On an incomplete review, the /review comment goes through write() (rehearsed in DRY), but s.reasked = {head, run} and s.waitFrom are saved unconditionally before the DRY exit. After a dry run on live state (the PR's own evidence: a dry run on #96 'chose ask Qodo ... again, then wait'), the next real run gets reaskPlan 'wait' for a new run nobody requested, never posts /review, and stops after reviewWaitMin. Rule 7: nothing is marked posted until GitHub shows it (#60). Whether the runner already asked should come from the PR's comments (a /review after the push), not a local note.

findings.title: An /agent retry written on the ticket for an earlier run resumes a new run
findings.why: A fresh run's state (line 611) has no lastAsk, and the ticket-resume loop takes every owner /agent comment on the ticket with id > (s.lastAsk || 0). On a re-labelled ticket (e.g. #96, run several times) any old '/agent retry' left on the ticket resumes the new run on the next tick after any pre-push stop. The owner didn't ask for that, the stop is overridden before they see it, and it uses up a retry round. Asks should count only if they come after this run's stop (or the pickup should set lastAsk to the newest comment).

findings.title: A dry run uses up the owner's /agent retry on the ticket without doing it
findings.why: The new ticket-resume loop has no DRY check: it saves s.lastAsk past the retry, increments retryRounds and sets phase 'work', then runs checkAndPush. In DRY, agent() throws 'DRY RUN stops here' (or the push is faked, giving s.pr = 0 from the fake URL), stop() saves phase 'help', and the real runner never sees that retry again. Rule 7, #53: lastAsk moved past an instruction that hasn't been carried out.

findings.title: The flaky note can list no failing lines
findings.why: testRetry builds the note from first.fails only. A first run killed by the spawnSync timeout or exiting non-zero with no FAIL/✖/AssertionError line has fails = [], so the PR proof says 'failed once' without the lines that failed, which the ticket asks for. Falling back to the tail of first.out would cover it.

findings.title: A failure with an empty second-run output reports the first run's output
findings.why: `second?.out || first.out` and `second?.fails || first.fails` fall back to the first run whenever the second run's output is '' (for example the sandbox failing to start). The agent is then given the first run's lines as if they came from the latest run. Use `second ?? first`.
